title: Skill Onramp Experiment Protocol & Mentor Runway
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a lightweight, measurable experiment for hiring mid-level ICs using a short trial + structured mentor runway. Goal: reduce time-to-productivity, improve conversion signal, and lower false positives for hires who need strong cross-functional onboarding support.

Hypothesis
If we run a 48-hour paid micro-trial followed by a 30-day mentor runway with defined success metrics, then (a) we will increase hire-to-retention by 15% for IC roles with heavy product/infra interplay, and (b) we will reduce new-hire time-to-first-meaningful-contribution by 40%.

Scope & target roles
- Target roles: Associate/IC-2 levels in eng-platform, observability, and developer-experience.
- Exclude senior IC (staff+) and purely frontend/product-design roles for this pilot.
- Pilot cohort size: 10 candidates (rolling, Q4 2025).

Experiment flow (high-level)
1) Screen -> short take-home (48h micro-trial) -> score -> offer trial contract -> trial week (paid 48h)
2) Trial evaluation (pass/conditional/fail) -> convert to 3-month hire with 30-day mentor runway + outcome review
3) Metrics captured continuously and at 30/90 days

Details: 48h micro-trial format
- Length: up to 48 hours total spread over 3 calendar days (candidate chooses cadence).
- Deliverable: small, scoped task (design + prototype + 200–400 word rationale) that mirrors day-1 work — e.g., instrument a simple endpoint, add a lightweight integration test, and write a short runbook.
- Acceptance criteria: clarity of tradeoffs, minimal working prototype, test(s) that demonstrate the approach.
- Assessment: independent reviewer + peer reviewer (synchronous pair for 45m optional).
- Compensation: $350 (paid on trial completion).

Interview rubric (used across screen, trial, and onsite)
- Criteria (scored 1–5):
  - Problem framing & tradeoffs (1–5)
  - Practical engineering (shipping-oriented) (1–5)
  - Testability & reliability thinking (1–5)
  - Cross-team communication (clarity + stakeholder empathy) (1–5)
  - Learning velocity (evidence of quick iteration) (1–5)
- Passing rule: average >= 3.6 and no category < 3 for conversion from trial -> hire.
- Notes to assessors: favor signal from shipped-oriented changes over academic correctness. Use examples: what would you change under high latency budget? how would you signal failure to product?

Mentor Runway (30 days): structure & responsibilities
- Mentor pairing: 1 mentor (peer-level) + 1 onboarding buddy (logistics, access) assigned day 0. Mentor ideally from the same pod but can be cross-pod with overlap.
- Week 0 (first 5 working days): orientation checklist + mentor shadowing sessions (3x 90m) + 1 small scoped production-task owned by hire (mentor co-pair).
- Week 1–2: increasing ownership, daily standups with mentor for 10–15m, two async feedback entries per week from mentor.
- Week 3–4: mentor gradually steps back; hire leads a small delivery and completes a retrospective with mentor and product partner.
- Mentor duties (explicit): set weekly learning objective, unblock infra access, pair on two PRs, give structured written feedback at day 10 and day 30.

Onboarding checklist (practical, prioritized)
- Pre-day0: accounts provisioned (github, ci, slack, vpn), sample runbook links shared, micro-trial artifacts included in onboarding kit.
- Day0: intro + expectations doc, meet mentor + buddy, run local dev environment, smoke test production read-only dashboard.
- Day0–5: complete 3 onboarding tasks (issue triage w/ mentor, small fix, add a test).
- Day6–30: two feature/bug cycles owned, join 2 product planning sessions, schedule 1 cross-team intro.

Evaluation & success metrics
- Conversion rate from trial -> hire (baseline to beat: internal historical 55% for these bands).
- 30-day time to first meaningful contribution (merge to main + production monitor) — target < 18 days.
- 90-day retention signal and manager satisfaction (NPS-like 1–5).
- Hiring funnel metrics: time-to-fill, cost-per-hire (trial compensation + recruiter time), interview-to-offer.

Feedback loops during pilot
- Weekly sync: people-ops + hiring manager + 1 mentor rep + recruiting lead.
- Retro at cohort end: what tasks predicted long-term success, which rubric items correlated with 90d outcomes.
- Quick experiments: swap deliverables, try pair-programming trial variant, evaluate paid vs unpaid trials for signal quality.

Risk & compliance notes
- Legal review required for paid trial wording in offer letter (JIRA: HR-4821).
- Compensation must be processed as contractor payment and reported to payroll taxonomy for 2025.
- Inclusive design: ensure trial tasks do not advantage candidates with existing infra at home (offer canonical sandbox environment).

Open questions (TBD)
- Should trials be anonymous at first pass to reduce bias? tradeoffs with pair exercise.
- How to handle candidates who can’t commit 48 consecutive hours due to timezone / caregiving constraints — allow asynchronous splitting (yes, default).
- Mentor bandwidth: what is the fair stipend / manager credit for mentors who invest 6–10hrs during runway?

Operational checklist for roll-out (immediate to Q4)
- [ ] finalize task templates for three teams (platform, obs, devx) — owner: Diego Morales — due 2025-09-20
- [ ] Confluence playbook + candidate-facing FAQ — owner: People Ops Docs — due 2025-09-25
- [ ] Legal sign-off on trial contract language — owner: Imani Brooks — due 2025-09-18
- [ ] Build sandbox environment and CI job to run candidate tasks — owner: infra-eng — due 2025-10-01
- [ ] Recruiter training on new rubric + scoring sheet — owner: Ravi Singh — due 2025-10-05
- [ ] Mentor stipend policy proposal — owner: Sophie Park — due 2025-10-10

Quick templates (copyable)
- Candidate invite blurb: "We run a short paid, take-home micro-trial to see real work fit. You’ll have up to 48 hours spread across 3 days and $350 compensation. If successful, we fast-track to a 30-day mentor runway and standard offer. More details: <link>"
- Mentor feedback prompt (day 10): "List 3 things hire did well, 2 areas to improve, and a suggested 30-day learning objective."

Notes to self / versioning
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic and experiment-first. Expect iteration after the first 5 hires. Keep the archive of trial deliverables and scored rubrics in github:repo/hiring-tooling/archives/Q4-2025 for later analysis.
- Next sync: 2025-10-08 weekly pilot review.

Appendix: sample scoring sheet (CSV-friendly row)
- candidate_id,task_score,problem_framing,engineering,tests,reliability,communication,learning_velocity,avg_score,pass_flag,assessor,trial_date
- Example row: C-1024,82,4,4,4,4,5,4,4.125,true,Mentor-Ravi,2025-09-30

End of doc.
